It is beautiful, well optimized, has great music, neat puzzles, and asks you question what the definition of a "person" is.

There are just so many reasons (for me) to love it.

It's an extremely well done puzzle game that looks nice, plays nicely and has a nice intro metaphysics story, a bit like The Swapper except The Talos Principle is a much bigger game. I think both are from the same writer, too. The dialogues and texts found throughout the game touch on a lot of topics, but the depth of the most cryptic reflections is easily lost if you don't know the material from another source already. The extension Road To Gehenna is basically a stand-alone that comes with its own set of philosophical inquiries, although arguably in an even more obscure package that would leave many with the false impression that the game tries to appear deeper than it really is. I would heartily recommend both, some of those puzzles are among the most difficult I have ever solved in a video-game, especially the special ones that you unlock after finding all stars. That said, some of the stars themselves are merely hidden which is a bit annoying and generally the only way to get them involves breaking the "rules" which isn't always as cool as it sounds.
